subject: french
title: Bigger Numbers
final_note: Big numbers for prices and ages.

walkthroughs.body_html: 20 vingt, 30 trente, 40 quarante, 50 cinquante, 60 soixante. After 60 things get unusual.
70 = soixante-dix (60+10). 80 = quatre-vingts (4 x 20!). 90 = quatre-vingt-dix (4 x 20 + 10). French does maths inside its numbers.
'I am 13' = J'ai treize ans. Notice you use 'j'ai' (I have) — French says 'I have 13 years', not 'I am 13'.

mcqs.q: How do French say their age?
When does the past participle agree with avoir verbs?
options: When the direct object comes BEFORE the verb (la pomme que j'ai mangée).
Either is fine in modern French.

mcqs.q: What tense follows 'depuis' for ongoing situations in French?
options: Past tense (because it is translated as 'have lived' in English).
Present tense (J'habite ici DEPUIS 5 ans - I have lived here for 5 years).

mcqs.q: When meeting a teacher or stranger for the first time, do you use 'tu' or 'vous'?
options: Tu, because it's singular and you're talking to one person.
Either is fine in modern French.
